subject: business-studies
title: Numbers in the Plan Adventure
welcome_lead: Words are nice — but plans need numbers. 📊
meta_desc: Business Plans Adventure 2 — KS3 Business Studies on forecasts, budgets and sales projections.
final_note: You learned about sales forecasts, budgets and how to spot risks in numbers.

walkthroughs.body_html:
A sales forecast guesses how much you'll sell.

Use research and similar businesses for clues. Don't be too optimistic — banks see through it. 👀

A budget is your spending plan.

List every cost: stock, wages, rent, ads. Stick to the total.

If actual costs go over → that's a variance. Fix it fast.

Smart plans show three numbers:

  • Worst case — flop.
  • Most likely.
  • Best case — viral.

If even the worst case still works, the idea is solid. 💪

mcqs.q: What is the difference between gross profit and net profit?
options: Porter's Five Forces are five physical security measures for a factory.
Gross profit = revenue minus cost of goods sold (direct costs only); net profit = revenue minus ALL costs including overheads, interest and tax. Net profit is the bottom line.
Gross profit and net profit are the same thing.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.

mcqs.q: What does Maslow's hierarchy of needs propose about motivation?
options: Humans are motivated by a hierarchy of needs (physiological, safety, social, esteem, self-actualisation) — lower needs must be substantially met before higher ones motivate.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
Maslow said employees must be promoted every year.
Maslow said money is the most important motivator at work.
